# Reference shirt virtual try-on

<a href="https://x.com/AdrianPunk115/status/2098055380857143807"><img src="https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HR22qgZbIAAF73P?format=jpg&amp;name=large" width="640" alt="Reference shirt virtual try-on — @AdrianPunk115 — Source result" loading="lazy"></a>

Apply a referenced shirt while preserving the subject, clothing construction, and printed details.

**Original prompt · Reference edit · Not independently tested**

### Required inputs

- Image 1: the subject reference.
- Image 2: the shirt reference.

<details>
<summary>Prompt</summary>



```text
Please place the top from Image 2 onto the person in Image 1 to generate a realistic virtual try-on image.

Image 1 determines the person's identity, body proportions, pose, camera angle, and background.
Image 2 determines the top's style, color, fabric, cut, pattern, and details.

Retain the person's face, hairstyle, skin tone, body shape, and original pose; replace only the top. Do not alter shoulder width, waist size, or body proportions simply to make the garment look better.

Accurately preserve the top's neckline, sleeve style, placket, pockets, buttons, and other visible structural elements.

Original prints, embroidery, logos, and text must remain in their corresponding positions on the garment. They may follow the natural curves and folds of the fabric but must not be altered, mirrored, added to, removed, or relocated.

The fabric should drape naturally over the shoulders, arms, and torso. Preserve the original fabric's thickness and surface texture; do not transform knitwear into smooth plastic or turn structured fabric into clingy, thin material.

Use a frontal view; do not display back-view designs not present in the reference image.

Retain the lighting and environment of the original image so the replaced garment blends in naturally. Output only a single try-on image; do not add text or "before-and-after" comparisons. **Please place the top from Image 2 onto the person in Image 1 to generate a realistic virtual try-on image.**

Image 1 determines the person's identity, body proportions, pose, camera angle, and background.
Image 2 determines the top's style, color, fabric, cut, pattern, and details.

Retain the person's face, hairstyle, skin tone, body shape, and original pose; replace only the top. Do not alter shoulder width, waist size, or body proportions simply to make the garment look better.

Accurately preserve the top's neckline, sleeve style, placket, pockets, buttons, and other visible structural elements.

Original prints, embroidery, logos, and text must remain in their corresponding positions on the garment. They should naturally curve and fold with the fabric but cannot be rewritten, mirrored, added to, deleted, or moved to other locations.

The fabric should drape realistically over the shoulders, arms, and torso. Preserve the original fabric's thickness and surface texture; do not turn knitwear into smooth plastic or transform stiff, structured fabric into clingy, thin material.

Present the garment from the front view; do not actively display back-view designs not provided in the reference image.

Retain the original image's lighting and environment so the replaced clothing blends in naturally. Output only a single "try-on" image; do not add text or "before-and-after" comparisons.
```

准确保留上衣的领口、袖型、门襟、口袋、纽扣以及其他可见结构。

原有的印花、刺绣、Logo和文字应位于衣服对应的位置。它们可以随布料产生自然弯曲和褶皱，但不能被改写、镜像、增加、删减或移动到其他位置。

采用正面展示，不主动展示参考图没有提供的背面设计。

保留原图的光线与环境，让替换后的衣服自然融入。只输出一张试穿图，不添加文字或前后对照。**请将图2中的上衣，穿到图1的人物身上，生成一张真实的试穿效果图。**
